claims.text: Standard casting or rapid solidification produces a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and exhibits brittle failure.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause the untreated alloy's brittle failure.
A short, low-temperature anneal will relax internal stresses at phase boundaries.
Relaxing internal boundary stresses will reduce dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations.
The proposed treatment will significantly improve room-temperature tensile ductility.
The proposed treatment will retain or slightly increase strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed intervention is annealing at approximately 400 °C for 10 minutes in argon, followed by rapid quenching.
Annealing in argon prevents oxidation during processing.
The predicted benefit applies to room-temperature tensile testing at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1 in laboratory ambient conditions.
The anneal will cause partial stress relaxation at lamellar colony boundaries.
The anneal will cause minor recrystallization or restructuring at lamellar colony boundaries.
Boundary restructuring will produce more compliant interfaces with less dislocation pile-up accumulation.
Low-temperature annealing enables local atomic rearrangement and slight recrystallization at phase boundaries.
Softer or more continuous boundaries will delay microcracking.
The treatment will preserve the microstructural features responsible for high strength.
Excessive annealing can over-coarsen the microstructure.
Insufficient annealing may fail to relieve interfacial stresses adequately.
